clean.query: What type of boat was the German submarine U-505 that was captured by the U.S. Navy in 1944?

docs.title: German submarine U-505
docs.text: U-505 is a German Type IXC U-boat built for Nazi Germany's "Kriegsmarine" during World War II.  She was captured by the U.S. Navy on June 4, 1944.

docs.title: Zenon B. Lukosius
docs.text: Zenon B. Lukosius (August 24, 1918 – August 12, 2006) was a Lithuanian–American World War II veteran who was a member of the U.S. Navy crew that captured the German submarine U-505, in 1944.  This was the first time that the US Navy had captured an enemy ship since the nineteenth century.  More importantly the Americans captured a code book that enabled Allied forces to more frequently pinpoint other German vessels.

docs.title: German submarine U-758
docs.text: German submarine "U-758" was a Type VIIC U-boat built for Nazi Germany's "Kriegsmarine" for service during World War II.  Commissioned on 5 May 1942, she served with the 6th U-boat Flotilla until 1 November as a training boat, and as a front boat until 14 October 1944 mostly under the command of "Kapitänleutnant" Helmut Manseck before joining the 33rd U-boat Flotilla as a training boat for the remainder of her service in the war.

docs.title: German submarine U-78 (1940)
docs.text: German submarine "U-78" was a Type VIIC submarine of Nazi Germany's "Kriegsmarine" during World War II.  She was the only German submarine to be sunk by land-based artillery fire during the war.

docs.title: USS Guadalcanal (CVE-60)
docs.text: USS "Guadalcanal" (CVE-60) was a "Casablanca"-class escort carrier of the United States Navy, which served during and after World War II.  She was the first ship to carry her name.  She was the flagship of the Hunter-killer Group which captured the German submarine ("U-boat") "U-505" .

docs.title: German submarine U-5269
docs.text: German submarine "U-5269" was a Type XXVIIB "Seehund" midget submarine which bears one of the highest registry numbers of the Kriegsmarine to be issued to a submarine during World War II.  "U-5269" was not, however, the last German submarine commissioned (that boat was "U-4712") but was issued a higher registry since contracted boats were frequently commissioned out of order due to scheduling and construction conflicts.

docs.title: HMS Bulldog (H91)
docs.text: HMS "Bulldog" (H91) was a B-class destroyer built for the Royal Navy (RN) from 1929 to 1931.  Initially assigned to the Mediterranean Fleet, she was transferred to the Home Fleet in 1936.  During the Spanish Civil War of 1936–1939, the ship spent considerable time in Spanish waters, enforcing the arms blockade imposed by Britain and France on both sides of the conflict.  "Bulldog" saw service throughout World War II on convoy escort duty during the Battle of the Atlantic and in the Arctic.  Her most notable actions were the capture of a complete Enigma machine and codebooks from the German submarine "U-110" in 1941, and sinking another German submarine in 1944.  The surrender of the German garrisons of the Channel Islands was signed on 9 May 1945 aboard "Bulldog".  Redundant after the war, she was broken up for scrap in 1946.

docs.title: SM U-90
docs.text: SM "U-90" was a Type U 87 u-boat of the Imperial German Navy during World War I.
